channel.description: Latest articles from The Beverly Hills Courier (beverlyhillscourier.com)

item.title: Hunt-Coffey and Gohlich Take Stage at ‘Straight Talk with Sharona’
item.description: During the final “Straight Talk with Sharona” of her mayoral term on March 12, Beverly Hills Mayor Sharona Nazarian hosted a panel with outgoing City Manager Nancy Hunt-Coffey and incoming City Manager Ryan Gohlich to discuss their priorities for Beverly Hills.

item.title: Planning Commission Approves Permits for Chabad of North Beverly Hills
item.description: The Beverly Hills Planning Commission at its March 12 meeting conditionally approved a request from Chabad of North Beverly Hills for the renewal of conditional use, extended hours and historic incentive permits to establish a religious institution at 9145 Wilshire Blvd.

item.title: BHPD Warns of Check Scam Ahead of Tax Season
item.description: The Beverly Hills Police Department (BHPD) is alerting residents and business owners to a serious financial scam involving IRS tax payment checks that are stolen from the mail and fraudulently altered.

item.title: Ovasapyan Named New Deputy Director of Community Services
item.description: The city of Beverly Hills has named Adrine Ovasapyan as the new Deputy Director of Community Services.

item.title: Chamber Hosts Women Who Shine Event
item.description: Businesswomen, female entrepreneurs and women leaders gathered at The Maybourne Beverly Hills on March 18 for The Beverly Hills Chamber's Women's Business Network's 4th Annual Women Who Shine: International Soirée.

item.title: City Council Votes 5-0 to Approve 26-Story Burton Way Project
item.description: The Beverly Hills City Council at its March 24 regular meeting voted unanimously to conditionally approve a development plan review and density bonus permit for a proposed 26-story mixed-use building at 8844 Burton Way that utilizes the state's Housing Accountability Act Builder’s Remedy provisions.

item.title: Southeast Area Residents Express Grievances at City Council Special Meeting
item.description: The Beverly Hills City Council hosted a special meeting for the city’s southeast area at the La Cienega Community Center on March 23 to discuss resident concerns and safety protocols for the upcoming Metro station at Wilshire and La Cienega boulevards.

item.title: BHUSD Approves Student Screen Time Guidelines
item.description: The Beverly Hills Unified School District (BHUSD) Board of Education approved new guidelines for student screen time at its March 24 meeting in a 3-2 vote, with Board Members Amanda Stern and Rachelle Marcus dissenting.

item.title: Commission Approves Modern, Multifamily Development on Durant Drive
item.description: The Beverly Hills Architectural and Design Review Commission approved the architectural review of a new 29-unit multifamily residence at 9945 Durant Drive in a 3-1 vote March 18, despite significant pushback from surrounding neighbors.

item.title: Fire Department to Hold Community Meeting Ahead of Second Evacuation Drill in May
item.description: The Beverly Hills Fire Department will conduct an informational community meeting on March 30 from 6-7 p.m. in City Hall’s Municipal Gallery to educate the community on how to be prepared to evacuate their homes during an emergency.

item.title: New Fees Will Offset Impact of Future Developments
item.description: The Beverly Hills Planning Commission at its March 26 meeting heard an update on the Development Impact Fee Nexus Study, which is being conducted by the city's Planning Division and a project consultant, Economics & Planning Systems, Inc. (EPS).

item.title: State Senator Ben Allen Addresses Rotary Club
item.description: California State Senator Ben Allen, who represents Senate District 24, addressed the Rotary Club of Beverly Hills luncheon on March 30.

item.title: Stephanie Harris Brings Community Perspective to Assistant City Manager Role
item.description: Director of Community Services Stephanie Harris was selected to serve as the next Assistant City Manager for Beverly Hills, joining incoming City Manager Ryan Gohlich’s office in July, following the retirement of City Manager Nancy Hunt-Coffey.

item.title: Thousands Gather at Beverly Gardens Park for ‘No Kings’ Rally
item.description: Around 2,000 people gathered at Beverly Gardens Park on March 28 as part of nationwide “No Kings” rallies protesting President Donald Trump. Organized by the American Civil Liberties Union, Indivisible, and numerous labor unions and grassroots organizations, the protest was one of dozens held throughout Los Angeles County.
